title: Redwood PLG Quickstart Discovery - StrataLabs
summary: Initial PLG-focused discovery. Customer is evaluating Redwood hosted quickstart for low-friction integration and wants to understand free credits, time-to-first-token, and migration path to Dedicated/Private. Security/compliance (SOC2, SSO, KMS) and cost/latency tradeoffs are primary concerns. Agreed to a short pilot with benchmarking and shared security docs.
next_steps: Redwood: send quickstart guide + sandbox creds
Redwood: share SOC2 + security architecture doc
StrataLabs: provide sample prompt set and perf/latency SLOs
Schedule bench run next week with Ethan and Priya
action_items: Maya (AE): send quickstart guide, sample curl + SDK snippets, and free credits link by EOD 2026-11-10
Ethan (SE): schedule bench test and request sample data from Priya; come prepared with recommended model/quantization options
Alex (CTO): share timeline for decision (end of November) and internal stakeholders list
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for making time. I'm Maya, AE on the Redwood team, with Ethan our solutions engineer. quick intro from you all?
[00:12] Alex (Strata CTO): Hey Maya, Alex here, CTO at StrataLabs. Priya's on for ML, Daniel on infra and Sana on product.
[00:18] Maya: awesome, thanks. Goal today is to walk through the PLG quickstart, time-to-first-token, and where customers typically land between hosted, dedicated, or private. Also want to surface any security or procurement constraints.
[00:30] Priya (ML Eng): quick note—we're primarily evaluating for a customer-facing assistant feature, about 3M tokens/day expected eventually, but initial POC is small. Key is latency under 300ms for short chat queries and cost predictability.
[00:50] Ethan (Redwood SE): got it. PLG quickstart is designed for that — self-serve signup, free credits, and a sandbox API key so you can get to first token within minutes. For production at your scale you'd likely evaluate Dedicated or Private for predictable throughput and isolation.
[01:10] Daniel (DevOps): can you explain the difference? we have strict data residency and internal compliance, so curious what the hosted quickstart means for data staying in our control.
[01:25] Maya: totally. Hosted is our managed API — data is processed transiently and customers can opt in to different retention policies; we offer SOC2 Type II and can route requests to regionally isolated infra. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and capacity guarantees; Private (VPC/on-prem) gives you full control over networking and KMS.
[01:45] Alex: and the free credits — are they usable against Dedicated too or just hosted?
[01:50] Maya: free credits apply to the hosted sandbox. For Dedicated/Private there's typically a different procurement path and reserved commits. That said, most teams start in hosted to validate product flows and then move to Dedicated when they need SLAs.
[02:10] Priya: how long to first token realistically? we have engineers who need something in a day or two.
[02:15] Ethan: from signup to first token with the quickstart flow it's often under 15 minutes if you follow the SDK/curl examples; if you bring your own model or custom infra it'll take longer. We'll send a quickstart guide with exact steps.
[02:30] Sana (Product): any sample integration? we use serverless backend calling APIs.
[02:35] Maya: yes, we have example node/python snippets for serverless patterns, plus a quickstart template that wires auth, streaming, and basic caching. We'll share a repo link in the follow-up.
[02:50] Daniel: infra question — KV cache and batching — how much control do we get? we want to batch a lot to save costs but can't increase tail latency.
[03:05] Ethan: runtime supports continuous batching and prefix/KV caching. You can configure batch windows and cache TTLs; for latency-critical endpoints you can pin to a lower batch size or route to a latency-optimized pool. There's also automatic routing to lower-latency machines for hot paths.
[03:30] Alex: security — SSO, SAML, audit logs, KMS? we need to integrate with Okta and manage keys.
[03:40] Maya: we support SSO (SAML/SCIM), RBAC, and integrations with customer KMS for Private deployments. Hosted offers encrypted-at-rest and in-transit with Redwood-managed keys by default, and customer-managed KMS is available on Dedicated/Private. We have audit logs and retention options — we'll share our SOC2 and security architecture doc.
[04:05] Priya: what's the tradeoff between hosted and dedicated on perf/cost?
[04:10] Ethan: hosted is easiest to get started and often cheaper at very low scale due to multi-tenant efficiency. Dedicated reduces noisy neighbor variability and lets you optimize quantization/instance types for your workload — usually lower unit token cost at scale but with commit requirements. Latency is typically better and more predictable on Dedicated because you can reserve capacity.
[04:40] Alex: any benchmarks you can share for similar chat workloads?
[04:45] Maya: yes we'll attach benchmark spreadsheets — typical P95 latencies and token cost estimates. we'll also propose a bench run with your prompt set.
[04:56] Sana: procurement — what's the purchasing cadence for Dedicated?
[05:00] Maya: monthly or annual reserved capacity contracts, we can do pilot credits and a short-term demo Dedicated if needed for benchmarking; enterprise pricing and add-ons for observability are separate.
[05:18] Priya: for model compatibility — we currently prototype on open models like Mistral and Llama variants — does Redwood host those?
[05:25] Ethan: we maintain a model catalog with curated open models and verified performance profiles; we'll check the specific variants you use. We also support running custom weights in Private deployments.
[05:40] Alex: latency target again — 300ms for short queries — is that realistic on hosted?
[05:46] Ethan: short answer: sometimes. It depends on sequence length, concurrency, and load. For reliable sub-300ms P95 you'd probably want Dedicated with latency-optimized instances and smaller context lengths; we can test that in the bench run.
[06:05] Daniel: any limits on tokens or quotas on the quickstart?
[06:10] Maya: sandbox keys come with a free credits pool and daily rate limits to prevent abuse; if you need higher throughput in sandbox we can temporarily bump quotas for the pilot.
[06:22] Alex: compliance question — do you support data residency in eu and us?
[06:25] Maya: yes, regional routing is available and for strict residency you'd use Dedicated with region pinned or Private.
[06:35] Priya: operationally — how are rollouts handled? can we do canary and A/B tests?
[06:40] Ethan: yes, Redwood Console supports canary deploys, A/B routing, and automatic fallback policies, plus tracing hooks and per-route dashboards.
[06:52] Sana: we have a separate security review team — can you run a quick security Q&A or share docs?
[06:57] Maya: absolutely — we'll send SOC2, encryption docs, network diagrams, and the contact for our security solutions engineer.
[07:10] Alex: timeline — we're aiming for a POC by mid-November and decision end-of-month.
[07:16] Maya: that's tight but doable. We'll prioritize sending the quickstart materials and credits today and set up the bench next week.
[07:28] Priya: on bench testing — what's required from our side? sample prompts, expected SLOs, typical context lengths?
[07:35] Ethan: yes, sample prompt set, example payload sizes, concurrency patterns, and any hard SLOs (p95/p99) — we'll run hosted then optionally a Dedicated pilot.
[07:48] Alex: do you have telemetry for token-level cost breakdowns?
[07:52] Maya: yes — Redwood Console gives token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-route and per-model. That helps identify regression and optimize prompts.
[08:05] Daniel: any gotchas around billing or unexpected egress costs?
[08:10] Maya: network egress follows cloud provider charges but we try to surface those; for Private on-prem there is no egress to Redwood. We'll note typical billing patterns in the pricing doc.
[08:25] Sana: question — is there a self-serve migration path from hosted to Dedicated without code changes?
[08:32] Ethan: in most cases yes — the API and config are consistent. You might pin model versions and change routing policies, but SDK calls remain the same. Some infra plumbing (VPC peering, KMS configs) is needed for Private.
[08:50] Priya: can you quantify cost differences — ballpark?
[08:54] Maya: ballpark depends on model and quantization. We'll include token-cost estimates in the follow-up; typical rule-of-thumb is hosted cheaper at <50k/day but Dedicated becomes more economical at high sustained usage.
[09:10] Alex: demo request — can we get a short demo of quickstart flow?
[09:14] Maya: yes we can do a 20-minute demo, but for now let's get you up with the quickstart. I'll share the repo and the curl examples.
[09:25] Daniel: logging and SIEM integration? we need audit logs shipped to our Splunk.
[09:30] Ethan: we provide audit logs and can also configure log export to your SIEM for Dedicated/Private; on hosted there are options for log forwarding as well.
[09:45] Priya: model quality monitoring — do you support evals/regression alerts?
[09:50] Maya: Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring tied to prompt sets and evals, with regression alerts; we'll include an overview.
[10:05] Alex: any recent outages or incident history we should be aware of?
[10:09] Maya: we have standard status pages and an incident history; for enterprise deals we can share SLO metrics. We'll attach that in the follow-up.
[10:20] Sana: who will be our main contact for technical troubleshooting during pilot?
[10:24] Maya: Ethan will be your SE point for the bench and technical setup; I'll be your AE.
[10:30] Ethan: I'll set up a calendar invite for the bench run and include a pre-req checklist.
[10:35] Alex: great. If we move to Dedicated later, what's the procurement timeline?
[10:39] Maya: usually several weeks to sign PO for reserved capacity, depends on legal/finance. For pilot we can keep things on hosted and then run a short Dedicated bench if you want.
[10:50] Priya: question — can we bring our own model weights?
[10:53] Ethan: yes, in Private you can bring custom weights; we also support customer-uploaded models in Dedicated with appropriate security review.
[11:05] Daniel: are there observability hooks to tie tracing into our APM?
[11:08] Ethan: yes, tracing hooks and per-route dashboards with spans export; we can walk you through integration during the bench.
[11:20] [silence/muted]
[11:40] Maya: quick check — any blockers right now that would prevent the pilot?
[11:45] Alex: procurement ok for small pilot; security wants the SOC2 docs — that's the only blocker.
[11:52] Maya: we'll send those today.
[12:00] Priya: timeline for bench run next week ok — Priya and Ethan will pair on that.
[12:05] Ethan: I'll send the invite and pre-reqs.
[12:18] Sana: one more question on rate limiting during the pilot — will sandbox throttle us heavily?
[12:22] Maya: sandbox limits are conservative but we can temporarily increase them for bench.
[12:30] Alex: excellent. Any competitors we should be aware of? we've been talking to OpenAI and Anthropic for hosted APIs, and evaluating self-host options like Replicate.
[12:40] Maya: understood; our differentiator is focused runtime and predictable economics plus a migration path to Dedicated/Private.
[12:55] Priya: can you include example quantization recommendations for Mistral/llama variants?
[12:59] Ethan: yes — we'll include model/quantization suggestions based on your prompt lengths.
[13:10] Maya: recap and next steps: we'll send quickstart + credits, SOC2/security docs, bench invite, and ask StrataLabs to share prompt set and SLOs.
[13:22] Alex: that works. anyone else?
[13:25] Sana: no, thanks.
[13:27] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up by EOD.
[37:30] [call ends - total 38 minutes]
